Hillary Clinton suggested that Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney may now be the leader of the free world, a title traditionally reserved for the president of the United States.

The former secretary of state made the remark during an interview with MS NOW’s Rachel Maddow at the Temple Emanu-El Streicker Center in New York to promote Maddow’s new book about the Justice Department, “Department of Fate.” The conversation aired on MS NOW on Saturday.

Maddow asked Clinton: “Do you think that there is a leader of the free world right now?”

“Maybe Mark Carney,” suggested Clinton, whom Donald Trump defeated in the 2016 election, drawing loud applause from the audience.

Watch here:

“That’s what I was going to ask,” replied Maddow, who said Carney is “certainly articulating a vision of the free countries of the world and of the liberty-loving nations of the world that is about being stronger together.”

Clinton, reflecting at another point in the interview on the record number of Democratic women elected in the 2026 midterms, also said she was “looking forward” to Trump delivering his next State of the Union address to a joint session of Congress “and he has to walk down that aisle and all these Democratic women are just staring at him.”

“It will be a sight for sore, sore eyes,” she said.

Clinton further described Democrats’ sweeping success in the midterms as “a long time coming” and said it was as if “the blue wave has washed away the poisonous cloud we’ve been living under for the last 10 years.”
